nodes.name: CoSA/CNT Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Before the synthesis of CoSA/CNT, carbon papers were sonicated for 10 min with ethanol and deionized water to guarantee a clean surface. The CoCl₂ solution (0.6 mmol in 6 mL ethanol solvent) was sprinkled onto carbon papers (25 × 55 cm²) at 65 °C by the ultrasonic spray coating machine. The obtained carbon paper was inverted and placed on a crucible containing C₃N₄ powder (3 g) and then pyrolyzed in a nitrogen atmosphere for 3 h at 800 °C with a heating rate of 5 °C min⁻¹. The C₃N₄ was prepared via the reported synthetic technique.[24] The formed product was etched with hydrochloric acid (6 M) for 24 h at room temperature, and then the CoSA/CNT catalyst was obtained.

nodes.name: Ru Deposition on CoSA/CNT
nodes.procedure: The acquired CoSA/CNT was added to H₂O solution with RuCl₃ (0.225 mmol, 30 mL) and rested at room temperature for 1.5 h. Then, the pH of the above solution was adjusted to 7 by injecting the NaHCO₃ solution (0.3 M) into it and the mixture was rested for 24 h at room temperature. As the reducing agent, the NaBH₄ solution (5 wt.% 5.625 mL) was slowly introduced to the suspension at 80°C and maintained for 2 h. Finally, the solution was filtrated and freeze-dried to obtain Ru/CoSA/CNT.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH using three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The HER activity of the different samples was investigated in a 1.0 M KOH solution using a three-electrode system. As seen in Figure 4a, the Ru/CoSA/CNT catalysts only required an overpotential of 15 mV to reach 10 mA cm⁻²... fitting Tafel slope of Ru/CoSA/CNT (33.3 mV dec⁻¹)... Ru/CoSA/CNT exhibited the smallest R_CT... highest C_dl (34.3 mF cm⁻²)... mass activity of Ru/CoSA/CNT was 11.3 times greater than that of commercial Pt/C... maintaining stability with no obvious degradation for over 1000 h at... 200 mA cm⁻² (Figure 4d).

The AEMWE device used a homemade NiFe-layered double hydroxide as the anode and Ru/CoSA/CNT as the cathode. Polarization curves at 80°C in 1 M KOH... reaches an industrial current density of 1 A cm⁻² at low cell voltages of 1.785 V... exhibits excellent stability over 100 h at... 500 mA cm⁻² with only slight decay (370 μV h⁻¹, Figure 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM examines morphology of CoSA/CNT catalysts verifying successful formation of carbon nanotubes on carbon paper.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were used to examine the morphology of the CoSA/CNT catalysts, which verified the successful formation of carbon nanotubes on carbon paper (Figure 2b, Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM of Ru/CoSA/CNT shows homogeneous dispersion of Ru atomic nanoclusters with diameter of 1.08 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A TEM image of the Ru/CoSA/CNT electrocatalyst demonstrates the homogeneous dispersion of Ru atomic nanoclusters on the CoSA/CNT surface (Figure 3a) with a small diameter of 1.08 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms atomically distributed Co single atoms on N-doped carbon framework in CoSA/CNT and Co SA sites near Ru ACs in Ru/CoSA/CNT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of atomically distributed Co sites on the N-doped carbon framework was confirmed by the presence of isolated brighter dots in the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of CoSA/CNT shows characteristic CNT peaks at ≈26° and 44° without visible metal diffraction peaks; Ru/CoSA/CNT shows no visible metallic Ru diffraction peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of CoSA/CNT shows characteristic CNT peaks at ≈26° and 44° without visible metal diffraction peaks (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS of CoSA/CNT shows peak at ≈1.45 Å ascribed to isolated Co-N bonds indicating single-atom CoN4 moieties.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS (Extended X-ray absorption fine structure) result for CoSA/CNT clearly displays a peak at ≈1.45 Å, which is ascribed to isolated Co-N bonds, suggesting that the majority of cobalt atoms in CoSA/CNT formed single-atom CoN4 moieties (Figure 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows CoSA/CNT contains ≈4.97 wt.% Co single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP results indicate that the CoSA/CNT catalysts contained ≈4.97 wt.% Co SAs (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/CoSA/CNT shows Ru 3p positive shift ≈1 eV and Co 2p negative shift ≈0.6 eV vs references, indicating electron transfer from Ru ACs to CoN4 substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the Ru 3p peak for Ru/CoSA/CNT displayed a noticeable positive shift (≈1 eV) compared with that of Ru/CNT. Similarly, the Co 2p binding energy of Ru/CoSA/CNT exhibited an obvious negative shift of ≈0.6 eV compared to that of Co/CNT.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows higher near-edge absorption energy than Ru foil; EXAFS shows Ru-N-Co (1.51 Å), Ru-Co (1.94 Å), Ru-Ru (2.35 Å) bonds indicating strong cluster-substrate interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra and fitting spectra of Ru/CoSA/CNT (Figure 3h; Figure S8 and Table S2, Supporting Information) indicate that the prominent peaks at 1.51, 1.94, and 2.35 Å represent the Ru-N-Co, Ru-Co, and Ru-Ru bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping of CoSA/CNT shows homogeneous dispersion of Co atoms; Ru/CoSA/CNT shows uniform distribution of Ru, Co, and N on CNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mapping image of CoSA/CNT demonstrates a homogeneous dispersion of Co atoms on the CoSA/CNT surface without Co aggregation (Figure 2c)... Element mapping further revealed that Ru, Co, and N were uniformly distributed on the CNTs (Figure S5, Supporting Information).
